title: Japanese for Convenience Stores in 9 Comic Scenes | Guess, Listen, Say It (Travel Japanese)
lead: From finding an item to paying at the counter, everything you need in a Japanese convenience store, in nine comic scenes. Guess first, then listen twice and say it.

intro.title:
Japan konbini
**9 phrases**
intro.say: Nine scenes in a Japanese convenience store. Guess each line before the answer.

phrases.label: Do you have this?
phrases.when: Can't find something? Show a photo and ask this.
phrases.tip: Showing a photo on your phone is the fastest way.
phrases.scene: In a snack aisle, Jiwoo holds up her phone with a photo of a snack bag on the screen and shows it to the clerk, who is stocking a shelf on the right; Minjun peers at the shelves behind Jiwoo.

phrases.label: Finding the ATM
phrases.when: Need cash? Ask where the ATM is.
phrases.tip: Many convenience stores in Japan have ATMs that take foreign cards.
phrases.scene: Near the store entrance, Jiwoo opens an empty wallet with a worried face and asks the clerk; the clerk smiles and points with an open hand toward a plain grey machine in the corner.

phrases.label: Using the restroom
phrases.ja: トイレを借りてもいいですか？
phrases.pron: Toire o karite mo ii desu ka?
phrases.when: Want to use the restroom? Ask first, like this.
phrases.tip: It's polite to ask the staff before you use it. Some stores don't have one for customers.
phrases.scene: At the end of the counter, Jiwoo leans in politely with a slightly urgent smile and asks the clerk; the clerk nods and gestures toward a plain door at the back.

phrases.label: Point card?
phrases.when: At the register, the clerk asks if you have a point card. If not, answer like this.
phrases.tip: You'll hear this question at almost every convenience store. A small wave of the hand works too.
phrases.hear: ポイントカードはお持ちですか？ (Pointo kaado wa omochi desu ka?) = Do you have a point card?
phrases.short: The question every konbini asks you
phrases.scene: At the checkout counter, Jiwoo has put a bento box and a drink down; the clerk behind the register asks a question, and Jiwoo answers with a small apologetic wave of one hand; Minjun stands behind her holding a bottle of tea.

phrases.label: Heating it up
phrases.when: To get a bento or a bun heated, say this.
phrases.tip: The clerk may ask first: atatamemasu ka. Then just say hai, onegai shimasu.
phrases.scene: At the counter, Jiwoo slides a bento box toward the clerk and points at a small microwave behind the counter; the clerk takes the bento with both hands.

phrases.label: Chopsticks
phrases.when: If you need chopsticks, say this.
phrases.tip: A spoon is supuun, a fork is fooku. Just swap them in for ohashi.
phrases.scene: At the counter, Jiwoo mimes eating with chopsticks with one hand while the clerk reaches under the counter for a pair of wrapped wooden chopsticks.

phrases.label: No bag
phrases.when: The clerk asks if you need a bag. If you don't, answer like this.
phrases.tip: If you do want one, say fukuro o kudasai. Bags at convenience stores usually cost a little extra.
phrases.hear: 袋はご利用ですか？ (Fukuro wa goriyou desu ka?) = Do you need a bag?
phrases.scene: At the counter, the clerk holds up a folded plastic bag with a questioning look; Jiwoo smiles, shakes her hand gently and opens her own cloth tote bag.

phrases.label: Paying by card
phrases.ja: カードでお願いします。
phrases.when: To pay by card, say this.
phrases.tip: Most convenience stores take cards and transit IC cards.
phrases.scene: At the register, Jiwoo holds out a credit card toward a small card reader on the counter; the clerk gestures toward the reader with an open hand.

bonus.label: Saying thanks
bonus.ja: ありがとうございます。
bonus.when: Finally, when you have paid, say thank you like this.
bonus.scene: Jiwoo takes her tote bag and the warm bento, bowing slightly with a smile; Minjun waves; the clerk bows back behind the counter.

outro.title: Recap: **9 phrases**
outro.say: All the phrases are in the description. Tell us in the comments how many you got right. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
